_meta.project: instex Instrument Explorer -- TELESCOPES mode: ESO Extremely Large Telescope (ELT, under construction) -- Nasmyth foci and the entrance pupil
_meta.companion: data/telescopes/elt.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows gmt.json: sources{key: cite, file, url}; elt: title, telescope (machine-readable mirrors, pupil, foci; refs point to sourced params as 'elt.<param>'), explorer_preset (the proposed web/tpresets.js entry), params, not_found, conflicts, notes.
_meta.rule: Each value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/telescopes/elt/. derived = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). figure_readoff = a value read off a saved figure or an image of a table (the caption or a nearby text quote is checked). NOT FOUND marks a gap. Nothing is filled from memory.
_meta.quote_normalization: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, primes, dashes, minus, multiplication sign (to x), division slash, tilde operator, approximately-equal sign, middle dot, plus-minus (to +/-), the degree sign and the superscript-zero degree glyph normalized; whitespace collapsed; a quote also passes against the text with PDF line-end hyphenation removed or closed up, or with all whitespace removed; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces.
_meta.texts_checked: pdftotext -layout and -raw per page and across consecutive page pairs (PDF p. = page index of the saved PDF); HTML as tag-stripped text (tags to a space, tags removed) and raw source (UTF-8); .py and .tbl as is.
_meta.pupil_frame: ESO M1 frame of the Construction Proposal Fig. 3.66 (meters in the entrance pupil, angles from +X_M1); orientation relative to the elevation axis NOT FOUND
_meta.design_vs_asbuilt: Current design: ESO ELT web pages (EMIR, EM1, EM23, EM4, EM5, EST, EPFS, EF), Messenger 2018-2024 (C18, C19, V19, V21, V24), P23; ICD ESO-253082 values only through third parties (R18 v3.6, A24, IRDBM/IRDBC issue 4). 2011-2012 design: CP, C12, ESD, ESM, TLR. Pupil models: AnisoCADO, hcipy (third party).
_meta.check_result: 158 quotes checked against the saved files, 0 failures (2026-11-15); FIGURE READ-OFFs (C12 Fig. 1 tables, CP Figs. 3.50 and 3.66, C18 Fig. 3) are not text-checkable: their captions are.

segment_layout.derived: DERIVED (pure-Python lattice count, scratch script): six rings of 6k segments with k = 5-9 hold 6 x 35 = 210 segments (the deferred 'five inner rings'), so the full M1 starts at ring 5 and the center plus rings 1-4 (61 positions) stay empty. Keeping the lattice positions with ring >= 5 and center radius < Rc gives exactly 798 for 15.3948 < Rc/p < 15.5242 (AnisoCADO uses 15.4); the same rule with ring >= 10 gives 588 (C18's Phase 1 count). Per ring: rings 5-15 complete (30 ... 90), ring 16: 78 of 96, ring 17: 60 of 102; 133 per 60-deg sector. hcipy's 2011-based model, reproduced in pure Python from the saved source, also gives 798 segments, with center radii 4.359-15.395 pitches: the same set.

AnisoCADO: corners at 0, 60 ... deg, neighbors at 30, 90, 150 deg; each bar |X cos(phi) + Y sin(phi)| < w/2 with phi = 0, 120, 240 deg lies along phi + 90, i.e. arms at 30 + 60k deg: the same relation. In tpupil.js terms (rot 30 turns the pointy-topped lattice into flat-topped segments with rows at 30 + 60k): vanes at 30, 90, 150, 210, 270, 330 deg.
